MY LITTLE SCIENCE PROJECT

Parts of My Plant

Look for a seed, root, stem and leaf. Draw each part, name it and describe what it does.

A seed contains a young plant and stored food. Roots anchor the plant and absorb water and minerals. A stem supports the plant and transports materials. Leaves use light to help make food. Some parts may not be visible yet.

With a grown-up: use untreated planting beans; do not eat seeds or sprouts. Keep small seeds away from younger children. Wash hands after handling. An adult should discard any mouldy setup.

Read the complete growing guide ↗

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.

ACTIVITY 1

Choose a part

Word bank: seed · root · stem · leaf. Draw one part you can see.

ACTIVITY 2

Choose another part

Draw a different part and describe its job.

ACTIVITY 3

Look below the surface

If the roots are visible through your cup, draw them. Do not pull up the plant.

Your ideas belong here. There is no score.

What are we learning?

A plant has different parts with different jobs. Observing the real plant and explaining those jobs helps connect words with living things.
